text:
sam: Quick question for opinions  default validation pattern for the Console's multi-section forms (project create, feature flags). Inline-only, top-summary-only, or hybrid? Also how do we show required fields without clutter?

meera: Hybrid sounds best: inline for single-field fixes, top summary on submit when there are multiple errors or server-side failures. For required markers: subtle asterisk + legend on long forms.

ezra: Agree on hybrid. Small add: make top summary actionable anchors ("1. Name 3 jump to field"). When clicked it should focus the input and open any collapsed section.

carla: Accessibility nit: inline errors must be programmatically connected via aria-describedby and update an aria-live region so screen readers announce them on submit. Use aria-atomic="true" for predictable announcements.

toni: Regarding required markers, I'd avoid writing "Required" everywhere. Asterisk plus a top legend ("* required") for density. For complex inputs (schema, connection string) show a tiny persistent badge "Required" next to the label.

sam: What about destructive confirms? Ops recommends typed-confirm everywhere. UX wants less friction for devs. Thoughts on tiered strategy?

meera: Tiered SGTM: typed-confirm for resources tagged "production" or with external exposure, checkbox+warning for others, and optional countdown for intermediate risk. Document defaults so teams can opt-in stricter behavior.

ezra: If we allow countdown, ensure keyboard users can operate it and that it respects prefers-reduced-motion. Example: don't use a sweep animation that isn't keyboard-controllable.

carla: Modal semantics: role="alertdialog", aria-labelledby -> heading id, aria-describedby -> body id. For typed-confirm input include aria-label that repeats the instruction and set autocomplete="off". Also trap focus and return focus to the original trigger on cancel.

a11y-bot: Accessibility tips: 1) inline error region = aria-live="assertive" for blocking errors, "polite" for warnings; 2) ensure error text includes the field label (e.g., "Email 3 enter a valid email"); 3) asterisk must meet contrast and have aria-hidden="true" with sr-only text "required"; 4) typed-confirm inputs should use inputmode="text" and have clear aria-describedby.

sam: Microcopy: don't use generic "Invalid". Prefer pattern: "<Field> 3 <actionable instruction>". Eg: "Repo name 3 must only contain letters, numbers, dashes."

meera: Also add a small guideline: when server returns a domain-level error (eg duplicate name), show a top toast + open the related field with inline error. Include an error code for support.

ezra: Telemetry suggestion: record validation_mode (inline|hybrid|summary), delete_confirm_type (typed|checkbox|countdown|none), and delete_risk_level (low|medium|high). We'll use that to refine defaults.

toni: E2E test asks: focus moves from top-summary item to field, screen reader announces inline errors on submit, typed-confirm exact-match enforced, cancel returns focus, countdown respects reduced-motion.

carla: Small UI detail: reserve vertical space for helper/error text to avoid layout jumps. If both helper and error exist, show only error visually but keep helper readable to screen readers if helpful.

sam: Action list: sam -> update Figma with hybrid variants + delete-modal patterns (checkbox, countdown, typed); meera -> draft microcopy for 15 common fields; ezra -> telemetry + gating proposal; carla -> a11y checklist and code snippets; toni -> test matrix. I'll loop in PM for rollout timing.

meera: One more nit: error link copy should be specific, not "click here". Use "Fix name input" or "Edit email".

sam: Perfect. I'll push mocks and ping for a quick thumbs-up. :rocket:
